title: You are told when your member verification comes through
body: The map now tells you once when an admin verifies you as a member, even on a page you left open. Email too, if you gave an address.

title: Filter by how well the sender can be identified
body: A new chip row filters by how far the sender can be identified. One byte is a guess between 256 nodes, and it is what isolates a flood.

title: The target list shows repeater names again
body: The target list shows repeater names again. An id too short or too ambiguous to trust is still shown as an id, not guessed at.

title: A reception with no sender now shows the byte we heard
body: A one-byte route mark now reads as #64, not a dash. A hint, not an identity: 256 nodes share each value, and it no longer counts as Sender unknown.

title: Locate reads the whole signal field
body: Locate now weighs every reading, not only the strongest. Against nine measured repeaters the average miss went from 680 metres to 210. Still an estimate, not a fix.

title: Waiting receptions always get sent
body: Receptions waiting to be sent now go out with the radio unplugged too.

title: The map opens on the last 30 days
body: A first visit now opens on the last 30 days, because All time quietly capped at 50,000. The short ranges are no longer hidden when logged out.

title: The map keeps up with the drive
body: New receptions now appear on the map on their own while you drive.

title: Receptions reach the map on time again
body: One reception that will not send no longer holds up everything behind it.

title: Ignore a sender you do not want to see
body: A node that floods the map can now be silenced from the map itself, the way the app has always allowed. Ignore it from its popup or tick it in the new Ignored list in the bar, and its receptions leave the points, the hex heat and the target list at once. The list is yours alone: it stays in this browser and is not part of a link you share. Settings holds everything you have ignored, so you can bring a node back.

title: You can now filter a flood that has no sender
body: You can now filter on traffic with no sender. Direct only is called No path now.

title: Two more kinds of reception stay on the map
body: An advert that fails its signature and a packet we cannot read are now drawn, with no name on them. Unreadable ones get a new Unknown type filter.

title: Search the target list
body: The target sheet has a search field. Type part of a name, or the first characters of an id as it appears on the map and in the ticker, and the list narrows to what matches while you type. Clearing the field brings the whole list back; what you already picked stays picked either way.

title: The map keeps up when the log is large
body: The map redraws only what changed, so a large log no longer makes it lag.

title: The map says how far back it goes
body: When the map cannot fit everything in view, it now names the date it reaches back to instead of just saying capped.

title: Node names stop printing over each other
body: Node names that would overlap are left off. Tap the marker for the name.

title: The map shows everything the radio hears
body: Receptions we cannot pin to a sender are now kept and drawn, roughly three times as many points.

title: The position note gets out of the way on a phone
body: On a phone the position note now appears and fades instead of staying all session.

title: Zoom and attribution follow the theme
body: The map's zoom buttons and attribution now follow the theme.

title: The connect button always offers a way back
body: The connect button now matches the real state, so a dropped link offers a way back.

title: Readings from one spot draw one bar
body: Readings within ten metres now draw one bar instead of a flickering stack.

title: The marker key stops covering the receptions list
body: The marker key now shows on activation and fades, instead of covering the ticker.

title: Release notes in plain language
body: This panel now carries one short note per change you can notice.

title: What's new sits in Settings
body: What's new is now a tab in Settings, with the unread dot on the Settings button.

title: The position layer says why it is empty
body: The position layer now says why it is empty instead of just showing nothing.

title: 3D view reads correctly again
body: Pillars at the same spot collapse into one, and a bar's colour matches the flat map.

title: Low-battery warning matches the radio
body: The low-battery warning now fires when the firmware does.

title: SF8 nodes on the position layer
body: SF8 nodes are now drawn on the advertised-position layer, which only showed SF7.

title: A short tour for first-time visitors
body: The map now offers a short walkthrough, once, reopenable from the controls.

title: 3D camera can look along the ground
body: The 3D camera now tilts to 85 degrees, with a sky behind it.

title: The receptions ticker is readable at a glance
body: The receptions ticker rows are now sized to read at a glance while driving.

title: Advertised node positions on the map
body: An optional layer draws where nodes say they are. Self-reported, not measured.
